questions.stem: What is the correct order of layers in Medallion Architecture?
questions.explanation: Medallion Architecture processes data in multiple layers: Bronze, then Silver, then Gold Delta Lake tables.

questions.stem: In which kind of tables does Medallion Architecture sit?
options: CSV files on a file server
questions.explanation: Medallion Architecture is sitting in Delta Lake tables, with Bronze, Silver and Gold all being Delta Lake tables.

questions.stem: Why is the Raw layer normally not considered part of Medallion Architecture?
options: Because it is stored in the Gold layer
Because it is deleted after ingestion
Because it contains only aggregated data
Because it is totally raw source data, whereas Bronze, Silver and Gold are Delta Lake tables
Because Databricks does not support it
questions.explanation: The Raw layer hosts source data that cannot be pushed directly to Bronze, and it is totally raw rather than a Delta Lake table.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a standardisation transformation named for the Bronze layer?
options: Standardising date formats from different source systems
Fixing data types and column sizes
Performing CDC to extract delta or incremental data
Building data marts around business KPIs
questions.explanation: Bronze handles date standardisation, NULL handling, data type fixes and CDC; data marts around business KPIs belong to the Gold layer.

questions.stem: How do data models in the Bronze layer compare with the source systems?
options: They remain the same as the source systems
They are converted to a star schema
They are converted to Third Normal Form
They are flattened into a single wide table
They are replaced by a semantic layer
questions.explanation: At the Bronze layer, data models remain the same versus the source systems despite the standardisation transformations.

questions.stem: What happens in the Silver layer of Medallion Architecture?
options: Raw files are landed from source systems
Data is transformed into an Enterprise Data Warehouse, often in the Bill Inmon 3NF model
Data is archived to cold storage
questions.explanation: Silver is where data is transformed into the Enterprise Data Warehouse, not mandatorily but often in the Bill Inmon 3NF model.

questions.stem: Which layer hosts Data Marts or Semantic Layers focused on business KPIs such as Customer Analytics or Product Recommendations?
questions.explanation: Gold is where Data Marts or Semantic Layers come into the picture, focusing on business KPIs like Customer Segmentation and Inventory Analytics.

questions.stem: Which traditional layer sequence is Medallion Architecture said to be equivalent to?
options: Landing, Staging, Data Warehouse/Data Mart, Semantic/Aggregation Layers, Cubes
questions.explanation: The layers mirror the long-used Landing, Staging, Data Warehouse/Data Mart, Semantic/Aggregation and Cube layers.

questions.stem: What is described as the only real difference Databricks brought with Medallion Architecture?
options: It brought everything into the Data Lake, eliminating RDBMSs
It added a fourth Platinum layer
It removed the need for data standardisation
questions.explanation: The only difference is that Databricks has brought everything into the Data Lake, eliminating RDBMSs.

questions.stem: Where do most organisations prefer to land all source system data?
questions.explanation: Most organisations prefer to land all source systems' data in the Raw layer, a preference the author shares.
